quick_skim.title: SLICEChat: Progressive In-Encoder Token Pruning for Whole-Slide Pathology Language Models
quick_skim.abstract: Whole-slide pathology images (WSIs) contain gigapixel-scale visual content, creating a major scalability challenge for slide-level multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Existing approaches process thousands of patch tokens and typically apply compression only after slide encoding, leaving multimodal attention computationally expensive. We introduce SLICEChat, a slide-level MLLM that integrates progressive token pruning within a hybrid Mamba--Transformer slide encoder. Mamba layers enable efficient long-range propagation, while Transformer layers preserve global interactions as the sequence is progressively shortened. Between stages, language-supervised, region-aware pruning removes spatially coherent low-utility regions under a controlled keep-rate schedule, producing compact slide representations before multimodal fusion. On SlideBench VQA, SLICEChat achieves 79.84% accuracy on TCGA and 59.09% on BCNB cohorts, outperforming prior slide-level pathology MLLMs, and achieves the highest overall WSI-Bench metrics. It also provides competitive memory usage and the inference latency among the evaluated models. These results demonstrate accurate and computationally efficient multimodal reasoning over gigapixel WSIs.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Addresses gigapixel WSI scalability for MLLMs. Proposes SLICEChat with progressive token pruning inside a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder, using language-supervised region-aware pruning. Reduces computational cost while preserving slide-level task performance.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该论文针对全切片病理图像（WSI）像素级规模给多模态大语言模型带来的可扩展性挑战，现有方法在幻灯片编码后才压缩令牌，导致多模态注意力计算昂贵。作者提出SLICEChat，在混合Mamba-Transformer幻灯片编码器内部进行渐进式令牌剪枝，通过语言监督的区域感知剪枝逐步移除空间上连贯的低效用区域。实验表明该方法在显著降低计算开销的同时，保持了幻灯片级病理任务的性能，为WSI的高效多模态分析提供了新思路。
